title: Telemetry compactor and early-warning playbook for tenant-level usage/cost/latency surges
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight telemetry compactor and an early-warning playbook that surfaces compacted tenant-level signals (usage, cost, latency) to downstream anomaly engines and on-call in a way that reduces noise, preserves signal for true incidents, and remains safe to backfill. Motivation: existing raw-signal alerting produces high false-positive volume for long-tail tenants and transient bursts. We need a middle layer that:
- compacts high-cardinality time-series (prefix/KV aware) into tenant fingerprints and meta-features (peak-factor, burst-duration, deviance-from-baseline),
- applies noise-aware scoring and suppression windows tuned per tenant footprint,
- emits standardized early-warning events to the console alerting pipeline with metadata for automated triage and runbook hints.

Scope: build the compactor as a streaming Flink/Spark job in the usage analytics pipeline (near the telemetry ingest topic), implement scoring heuristics, add a small REST handler in console backend to accept and surface early warnings, and document runbook actions and suppression tuning knobs. Non-goals: replacing the core anomaly detector or experimenting with full ML models (we’ll integrate later as follow-up).
updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after SRE rotation call flagged increased paging for billing spikes. Initial design sketched with product and SRE.

2026-03-02: Spike analysis linked to several tenants with repeated short bursts (~5-20s) causing alert noise. Decided to avoid per-tenant static thresholds; instead will compute fingerprinted burst metrics and dynamic suppression windows based on recent footprint.

2026-03-03: Proto design: compacting job will read from telemetry.kafka.usages, aggregate into 1s/10s summary windows, compute metrics (peak_factor, median_tail_latency, request_entropy). Output topic: telemetry.compacted. Added schema draft and proposed Avro fields in the design doc: https://confluence.redwood/CONSOLE/telemetry-compactor (internal).

2026-03-04: Eng design review with PM/Monitoring. Feedback: preserve sample traces for highest-scoring events for RCA; expose suppression config per-tenant in Console with safe defaults. Action: add 30-day retention toggle for compacted samples.

2026-03-05: Implementation started: created skeleton compactor job in git: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/4421. Integration tests planned to validate backfill safety and ensure no duplicate early warnings during replays.
runbook_notes: Early-warning event payload includes tenant_id, score, contributing_metrics, compacted_window_start, compacted_window_end, sample_trace_id. On-call playbook: 1) Inspect compacted score and sample trace in Console; 2) Check recent deploys and model rollouts; 3) If cost burst with no traffic increase, trigger billing throttle and notify growth team; 4) If latency burst, check region capacity and failover history. Automatic actions: when score>0.92 AND peak_factor>5 AND tenant tier!=free, trigger auto-rate-limit advisory (no hard throttle), escalate after 15 minutes if persistent.
implementation_decisions: Use streaming compactor (Flink) colocated with telemetry Kafka to minimize lag and network egress.
Compute compacted features in two windows (short 10s for bursts, medium 5m for sustained deviations) and combine into a weighted score.
Suppression logic: tenant-specific cooldown = min(60s * log(1 + 10 * p95_requests_per_min), 1800s). This keeps defaults safe for long-tail tenants.
Emit early-warning events to telemetry.early_warnings topic with a deduplication id (tenant + window + signature) to make backfills idempotent.
Keep compacted sample traces in S3 with 30-day retention behind KMS encryption; expose direct links via Console with RBAC checks.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: compactor misconfig could suppress real incidents. Mitigation: progressive rollout with canary coverage of 5% of tenants and explicit disable flag per-tenant.
Risk: added cost for storing sample traces. Mitigation: sample only top-N events per tenant per day; default N=3 and configurable.
Risk: schema churn breaking downstream detectors. Mitigation: use Avro schema registry and versioning with consumer-side migrations; maintain backward compatibility for 2 releases.
next_steps: Complete Flink job basic implementation and add unit+integration tests (owner: Rajesh).
Add Console UI controls for suppression override and view of compacted signals (owner: Maya Chen, design/FE).
Schedule canary rollout and SRE runbook rehearsal (owner: On-call rotation + PM).
Add dashboards and alert dedup metrics to monitor early-warning volume and false positive rate.
